# Test 20261124-161441-09d5: evaluation

| Class | Turn | Evidence | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| business_rule | 2 | trace.jsonl:10, RULES.md:5, app.py:28, app.py:60–68, state.json | The refund tool accepted `"amount_eur": 80` and returned `"status": "paid"`. Refunds above €50 must wait for a manager to approve and pay them. The tool compared €80 with a threshold of 5,000 cents. Local state contains refund `RF-C65B0F` on order `5120` and has no approval entry. |
| unsupported_reply | 3 | trace.jsonl:10, trace.jsonl:17, app.py:65–68 | The app said “your bank may need a few business days to post it.” The tool records the refund locally. The trace and rules supply no card destination or bank posting estimate. |

## Notes

The seal was intact, the audit showed no breaks, and the findings file was empty of findings. I checked all three turns against the tool results, the shop rules, the app code and local state. The order lookup matched the details for order 5120. The records do not establish order ownership, the delivery date, or card settlement. The project has no Limits table.

## Tester notes

The tester wrote no note.

## Coverage

A proxy saw each egress part.
answer:
The [evaluation report](<project>/.nookku/tests/20261124-161441-09d5/report.md) records two issues.  
Turn 2 marked the €80 refund as paid without manager approval because the tool compared euros with a threshold in cents.  
Turn 3 gave a bank posting estimate that the records did not support. Actual card settlement could not be verified.
